verse.text: All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: that the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.

sermon.title: Patient in Spirit, Not Proud in Spirit
sermon.excerpt: Oppression can make a wise man act like a fool, and a bribe can quietly undo a good heart. Ecclesiastes names a steadier way to stand — patient in spirit, slow to anger, and willing to wait for the end before judging the beginning.

lines: Father, I refuse to let any pressure I am under bend my mind the way oppression bends a wise man toward madness. My wisdom belongs to You, and no weight I am carrying gets to take it from me!
I declare that nothing — no gift, no favor, no flattery — gets to quietly buy out my heart. My heart answers to You alone, and it is not for sale!
I will not judge this chapter before it is finished. The end of this thing is better than its beginning, and I trust the One who is writing the ending!
I choose to be patient in spirit today, not proud in spirit. I do not need to force a resolution on my own timeline — I can stand steady in what is unfinished, because You are still working!
I declare that I am slow to anger, in Jesus' name. Anger may visit me, but it will not rest in me — it has no home in my spirit, because my spirit belongs to the Prince of Peace!
I will be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to wrath, for the wrath of man does not work the righteousness of God in me or around me!
So today I lay down every hasty reaction and I pick up patience — the kind that is better than pride, the kind that outlasts pressure, the kind that waits for God to finish what He started!
If you have been pressed until your peace felt thin — hear this: the end of your story is still coming, and it is good. Do not let a hard beginning write your conclusion for you.
Save this. Speak it over every situation that is tempting you to rush or rage. Patient in spirit. Slow to anger. Trusting the end more than I fear the beginning. In Jesus' name, amen!
